biod: fix closed fake biometric pipe from live locking the message loop The named pipe used by FakeBiometric for input is added to the message loop in order for it to get signaled when there is input. Due to the way pipes work, a poll on their FD will always trigger a POLLHUP after the pipe is opened writable and closed, which fake_biometric_tool does. Because this constantly happens, no other events could make it through the message loop. The workaround is to open the pipe read/write in FakeBiometric to ensure a writable end is always open, which prevents POLLHUP. BUG=None TEST=send data using fake_biometric_tool and then send something via dbus-send and ensure a response comes without timing out Change-Id: I1552f3c93fc845c76d7e859baad1ec95cf0a36c9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/384638 Commit-Ready: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org> Tested-by: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org>

biod: add GetId() to biometric interface Due to some fun with race conditions and removing arbitrary Enrollments at any time, a stable ID is required to reference Enrollment objects on DBus. More specifically, the sequence below led to an issue 1) a client gets a list of enrollments, which originally were just named in order of the returned vector from GetEnrollments 2) removed enrollment N in the middle of the vector 3) removed enrollment N+1 Enrollment that was originally N+1 would actually be enrollment N after the removal, leading to unwanted results for the client. The usage of a stable ID supplied by the Biometric upon enrollment nicely sidesteps this problem. BUG=None TEST=Enrollment IDs don't change after removing an enrollment from a Biometric Change-Id: Iee65ef81d810e6a8159268f18659aa302d313a78 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/384640 Commit-Ready: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org> Tested-by: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org>

cr50: make device state detect level triggered The interrupts on all of the gpios detecting if the device is on were edge triggered. If the rising edge happened in between when the gpio level was read and when the interrupt was enabled, then the device state could be falsely detected as off for a short period of time. This change changes them to GPIO_INT_HIGH. glibc: add clang-style FORTIFY. This patch adds support for a clang-style FORTIFY to ChromeOS's glibc. Without this, when we swap to clang as the default compiler for ChromeOS, our FORTIFY story will get *way* worse. When given a gcc-style FORTIFY, clang is unable to emit just about any compile-time diagnostics, and the dynamic checks that clang emits is a (small) subset of gcc's. This patch makes clang's diagnostic story nearly on-par with gcc's, and should allow clang to dynamically catch just about any bug that gcc can (either statically or dynamically). Due to differences in how the compilers work (e.g. how they optimize code, etc.), there may be cases where clang detects errors at run-time where gcc can't and vice-versa.
